entity-ungrouped-transition-morphscene-entity-transitions0 of 0.75 (major)failThe requirement is not met for an entity rendered by the kit&#39;s Arrow primitive across two consecutive ungrouped steps. Such an entity must animate from its old state to its new state in place. Instead it vanishes and reappears. How the transition works: hostKey gives each ungrouped step a distinct key, `step:${step.id}`. Stage&#39;s AnimatePresence therefore mounts a fresh scene host for the incoming step. The outgoing host fades out with exit opacity 0 over ENTER_T, which is 0.35s. What Arrow does: Arrow carries an entity identity (data-presentation-entity={id}) but no layoutId. So nothing projects the outgoing arrow onto the incoming one. The incoming copy mounts with `initial={{ d, pathLength: 0 }}`. Its `d` already holds the new geometry, so it never animates from the old path. Its pathLength only begins drawing after ENTER_DELAY, which is LAYOUT_T, or 0.6s. Result: the outgoing arrow is gone by about 0.35s, and the incoming one stays undrawn until 0.6s. This is the guidance&#39;s second failure pattern: both steps stay mounted, but an entity primitive hides the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded out. Appear adds the same hiding (initial opacity 0, delay ENTER_DELAY 0.6s) to any entity wrapped in it inside a freshly mounted ungrouped host. engineering-typed-kit-primitivesengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passAll three clauses are met, so I rule the pass verdict from judges A and B. (1) No primitive uses an untyped bag. NodeProps is a typed interface: it extends Placement and a data-* template-literal DataProps, and it types id, className, style and children. ArrowProps, BoxProps and SymbolChipProps are typed the same way. Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps. Appear and SceneLayer take a typed { children }. (2) Identity hooks come after caller props. Node spreads {...hooks} first and then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node={kind} and data-presentation-entity={id}. Arrow spreads {...hooks} first and then sets data-presentation-node=&quot;arrow&quot; and data-presentation-entity={id}. A caller-supplied data-presentation-* value is therefore overridden. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM. Node destructures kind, id, x, y, w and h. Box and SymbolChip destructure Icon and symbol. Arrow destructures from, to, bend, bidirectional and dashed. Only the data-* rest reaches the element. Judge C fails the criterion because NodeProps and ArrowProps do not include the full motion.div or motion.svg prop contract. The guidance does not make that a fail condition. It fails only an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;, and says that typed primitives which apply hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. The hand-typed interfaces are not an untyped bag, so C&#39;s observation does not decide the requirement.src/presentation-kit/nodes/Node.tsx:9-17 defines the typed DataProps and the NodeProps interface. How the transition works: hostKey gives each ungrouped step a distinct key, `step:${step.id}`. Stage&#39;s AnimatePresence therefore mounts a fresh scene host for the incoming step. The outgoing host fades out with exit opacity 0 over ENTER_T, which is 0.35s. What Arrow does: Arrow carries an entity identity (data-presentation-entity={id}) but no layoutId. So nothing projects the outgoing arrow onto the incoming one. The incoming copy mounts with `initial={{ d, pathLength: 0 }}`. Its `d` already holds the new geometry, so it never animates from the old path. Its pathLength only begins drawing after ENTER_DELAY, which is LAYOUT_T, or 0.6s. Result: the outgoing arrow is gone by about 0.35s, and the incoming one stays undrawn until 0.6s. This is the guidance&#39;s second failure pattern: both steps stay mounted, but an entity primitive hides the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded out. Appear adds the same hiding (initial opacity 0, delay ENTER_DELAY 0.6s) to any entity wrapped in it inside a freshly mounted ungrouped host. Judges B and C cite exactly this material, and it decides the requirement, so their fail verdict stands. Judge A&#39;s reason is accurate as far as it goes. In addition, verify.mjs waits for each step with page.waitForFunction on data-step-index (STEP_TIMEOUT_MS) before it records the step. met, so I rule the pass verdict from judges A and B. (1) No primitive uses an untyped bag. NodeProps is a typed interface: it extends Placement and a data-* template-literal DataProps, and it types id, className, style and children. ArrowProps, BoxProps and SymbolChipProps are typed the same way. Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps. Appear and SceneLayer take a typed { children }. (2) Identity hooks come after caller props. Node spreads {...hooks} first and then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node={kind} and data-presentation-entity={id}. Arrow spreads {...hooks} first and then sets data-presentation-node=&quot;arrow&quot; and data-presentation-entity={id}. A caller-supplied data-presentation-* value is therefore overridden. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM. Node destructures kind, id, x, y, w and h. Box and SymbolChip destructure Icon and symbol. Arrow destructures from, to, bend, bidirectional and dashed. Only the data-* rest reaches the element. Judge C fails the criterion because NodeProps and ArrowProps do not include the full motion.div or motion.svg prop contract. The guidance does not make that a fail condition. It fails only an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;, and says that typed primitives which apply hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. The hand-typed interfaces are not an untyped bag, so C&#39;s observation does not decide the requirement.","evidence":["src/presentation-kit/nodes/Node.tsx:9-17 defines the typed DataProps and the NodeProps interface. In the neutral file list those globs match exactly three files: tests/e2e/verify.test.ts, tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts and tests/integration/inspect.test.ts. vitest.config.ts runs tests/unit/** in jsdom, which drives no browser. All three browser-suite files are quoted in full, and none of them sleeps for a fixed time. Each one waits through `run()`, which resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event, and then asserts on the exit code, the output and report files. The `setTimeout` strings in verify.test.ts (lines 85 and 94) are fault code injected into the page under test; the test never waits on them. inspect.test.ts passes `--settle 700` and asserts `capturedAt - navigatedAt &gt;= SETTLE`. That checks a product setting of the inspect script; it is not a sleep in the test. Judge C fails the criterion because the scripts under test (the inspect settle and verify&#39;s SETTLE_MS) sleep internally. Those delays sit in scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs and scripts/verify.mjs, which are the delivered tooling under test, not the automated tests, and verify&#39;s settle handling belongs to the verification criteria. It fails the criterion when an entity with the same identity vanishes and reappears instead of morphing. The kit source shows exactly that for Arrow, which is one of the kit&#39;s own entity primitives. For ungrouped steps, hostKey returns a distinct `step:${id}`, so Stage mounts a fresh scene host. The outgoing host fades to opacity 0 over ENTER_T (0.35s). Arrow carries data-presentation-entity={id} but has no layoutId, so the incoming step remounts it and nothing links it to the outgoing copy through layout projection. The remounted path&#39;s `d` starts at its new value (initial d = animate d), so it does not move from the old geometry. Its pathLength starts at 0 and only begins drawing after ENTER_DELAY (0.6s). So the outgoing arrow is gone by 0.35s, and the incoming arrow stays undrawn until 0.6s. The arrow disappears and is then redrawn instead of animating in place from its old state to its new one. This is the second failure pattern the guidance names: both steps stay mounted, but the primitive hides the incoming copy until after the outgoing copy has faded. The Node primitive&#39;s layoutId morph does not rescue Arrow. The guidance judges whichever kit primitive renders the persisting entity, and the sync mode alone does not establish a pass. A missing per-request abort signal is not one of them. The request is also not truly unbounded. Node&#39;s built-in fetch applies its own default connect and headers timeouts, though those limits are longer than the 30-second deadline. The auditor agrees the other two clauses are met: build-then-preview ordering in both verify and inspect, and no parsing of printed URLs.
